title: Tenant-safe retention blueprints and eviction-simulation playbook for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Customers need clear, tenant-scoped retention templates that cover interactive artifacts (prompts/responses), request logs, and derived telemetry (metrics/latency traces). Current retention controls are per-route and fragmented; teams report uncertainty about inheritance rules, legal-hold handling, and how evidence bundles are produced for compliance audits. We also lack a safe way for tenants to preview the operational effect of TTLs and sample policies before they impact live data.
tasks: Design a set of tenant-safe retention blueprints (Default, Business, Regulated, Minimal) that map TTLs for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
Define deterministic inheritance rules and explicit overrides for route/tenant/resource levels
Add an eviction-simulation engine in the Console that runs a dry-run over synthetic/real metadata to show items that would be purged/kept
Specify evidence export artifact format for each blueprint (manifest, hash-chain, residency tag) and attach to existing evidence pipeline
Collaborate with ENG to add hooks for legal-hold flags so items only excluded from purges and included in evidence bundles
Implement a small UX flow for operators: create blueprint, simulate eviction, approve and schedule enforcement
Author docs, README, and sample scripts for customers to adopt blueprints via API or Console presets
acceptance_criteria: Console exposes four tenant blueprint presets and allows per-tenant customization of TTLs for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
Eviction simulator produces a preview report with counts, size estimates, and residency-region impact for a selected time window
Evidence export includes signed manifest and residency metadata and can be triggered as part of scheduled purge runs
Legal-hold flag prevents deletion and forces inclusion in export bundles; documented fallback when conflicting holds exist
Migration path exists: preview mode can run against a tenant with no data deletion until 'enforce' is clicked; audit trail recorded
Automated e2e tests validate TTL inheritance, override precedence, and simulator correctness against sampled datasets
